title: kbmon_otel.py builds its signal exporters from one registry, and the otel and mon_ modules are mapped
goal: otel/kbmon_otel.py builds each signal's exporter from one SIGNALS registry, so a new signal is one module and one row; kb/_self/map.csv maps otel/*.py and _tools/mon_*.py to the docs that name them

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print('check failed:', e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import ast
t = ast.parse(open('otel/kbmon_otel.py', encoding='utf-8').read())
reg = [n for n in t.body if isinstance(n, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign)) and any(getattr(x, 'id', '') == 'SIGNALS' for x in (n.targets if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) else [n.target]))]
mains = [n for n in t.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == 'main']
direct = [c.func.value.id + '.' + c.func.attr for m in mains for c in ast.walk(m) if isinstance(c, ast.Call) and isinstance(c.func, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(c.func.value, ast.Name) and c.func.value.id in ('otel_logs', 'otel_spans')]
print('SIGNALS registry:', bool(reg), 'direct exporter calls in main:', direct)
sys.exit(0 if reg and not direct else 1)

    if p.returncode: bad.append(i)
print('still failing:',bad);sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
